title: Annotatio III §.X (2) close: Daily Mass-‘miracles’ vs the senses; Tillotson; Melchior — credible only by Enthusiasm; stop before (3)
pass_a_gloss: For since Christians are to believe miracles are wrought by God only rarely, not rashly nor for another end than that through them, as works surpassing every created finite power, most clearly exposed to human senses, they may be plainly convinced of the truth of what is hard to believe; Here indeed, or in the papistic Mass, on the contrary daily in countless times and places the same miracles are commanded to be believed repeated and recurring, against the most lucid testimonies of human senses fully convinced of the contrary. Compare Tillotson, Volume 3 of Sermons pp. 364–365. So that under this name Blessed John Melchior, not long since Doctor of Theology at Herborn, most ingeniously demonstrated Transsubstantiation credible only through Enthusiasm, Opera Theologica part 2 from p. 467 to 840.
pass_b_english: Miracles should be rare, not rash, to convince the senses of what is hard to believe; the papistic Mass instead commands the same ‘miracle’ daily in countless places against the senses’ clearest contrary witness (Tillotson Sermons 3, pp. 364–365).
Melchior of Herborn ingeniously showed Transsubstantiation credible only by Enthusiasm (Opera Theol. 2, pp. 467–840).
Stop before (3) Praxis Christiana (first table / latria; cup withheld).
source_text: Cum enim miracula rarò admodum, non temerè nec alio fine, à Deo patrari credenda Christianis sint, quam ut per ea, ceu omnem creatam finitamque potentiam supergressa opera, sensibus humanis clarissimè exposita, de veritate ejus, quod creditu difficile, planè convincantur; Hic quidem, seu in Missa papistica, è contrario quotidie innumeris vicibus, in innumeris locis, eadem repeti atque recurrere miracula, contra luculentissima sensuum humanorum de contrario plenissimè convictorum testimonia, credenda imperantur. Confer. Tillots. Volum. 3. Concionum p. m. 364. & 365. Ut hoc nomine perquam ingeniose B. Joh. Melchioris, non ita pridem Doctor Theologus Herbornensis, Transsubstantiationem, non nisi per Enthusiasmum, credibilem demonstraverit, Operum Theol. part. 2. à p. m. 467. ad 840.

lemmas.gloss: against the testimonies of the senses
